themes_detail.label: Street condition crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street Condition complaints spiked to 83 THIS WEEK vs. 14.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks—a 488% spike (z-score: 10.01)—suggesting rapid deterioration of road surfaces across Sheepshead Bay/Gravesend requiring immediate investigation into cause and scope.
evidence: 83 Street Condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 14.1 weekly average (488% increase, z-score 10.01)
Represents statistically significant deviation with high severity classification
Occurred simultaneously with other sanitation/infrastructure spikes, suggesting district-wide issue
reporting_angles: Ground truth: photograph and map affected streets; interview DOT on whether potholes/surface damage is localized or district-wide
Root cause: did recent weather, construction activity, or deferred maintenance trigger this spike?

themes_detail.label: Dirty streets epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Dirty Condition complaints jumped to 56 THIS WEEK vs. 16.5 weekly average—a 239% spike (z-score: 6.11)—concurrent with Street Sweeping Complaint surge (13 vs. 3.1 avg), indicating possible sanitation department breakdown or street cleaning service failure.
evidence: Dirty Condition complaints: 56 THIS WEEK vs. 16.5 weekly average (239% increase, z-score 6.11)
Street Sweeping Complaints: 13 THIS WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly average (316% increase, z-score 3.47)
Two converging 311 complaint categories suggest coordinated sanitation failure rather than isolated issues
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY on staffing, scheduling, or equipment changes in CD 315 this week; cross-reference with absences or service disruptions
Resident experience: talk to business owners and homeowners on heavily-spiked blocks about visible garbage, litter accumulation, and frequency of sweeping

themes_detail.label: Dead animals and pests surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead Animal complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average (229% spike, z-score: 5.26), and Illegal Animal Kept as Pet spiked 3 weeks ago (380% above baseline), suggesting possible pest infestation, wildlife conflict, or environmental contamination affecting public health.
evidence: Dead Animal complaints: 7 THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average (229% increase, z-score 5.26)
Illegal Animal Kept as Pet: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (380% increase, z-score 4.91)
Converges with Dirty Condition and Street Condition spikes, suggesting environmental degradation creating conditions for pest activity
reporting_angles: DOHMH investigation: are there known pest complaints, rodent sightings, or wildlife reports in same geographic cluster?
Environmental check: are dead animals concentrated near specific sites (construction, lots, water)? Could indicate contamination or disease outbreak

themes_detail.label: Litter basket infrastructure gap
themes_detail.summary: Litter Basket Request complaints exploded to 9 three weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average—a 1340% spike (z-score: 17.3, highest severity)—indicating residents perceive acute shortage of street litter receptacles or systematic removal/non-repair of existing baskets.
evidence: Litter Basket Request complaints: 9 (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.6 weekly average (1340% increase, z-score 17.3)
Highest z-score among all detected spikes, indicating extreme statistical outlier
Timing predates current Street Condition/Dirty Condition spikes, but may be root cause
reporting_angles: Inventory audit: DSNY data on number of litter baskets installed, removed, or out of service in CD 315 over past 8 weeks
Compare to other districts: is CD 315 basket-per-capita below citywide average? Is this part of targeted removal?

themes_detail.label: Restaurant violence and public safety
themes_detail.summary: A shooting incident at a Gravesend restaurant (March 16, 2026) in which a customer opened fire after ejection, injuring two, signals potential escalation of violent crime and conflict in local hospitality venues—context for broader safety trends in district.
evidence: Brooklyn Eagle report: shooting at Gravesend restaurant with 2 injured (March 16, 2026)
Incident involved escalation from ejection to gunfire, suggesting conflict management or security failure
No broader crime data provided, but notable violent incident in neighborhood during period of multiple infrastructure crises
reporting_angles: Follow-up on shooting investigation: arrests, charges, motive; any prior incidents at venue
Hospitality worker interviews: are restaurant staff reporting increased patron conflicts, aggression, or safety concerns? Is this part of broader trend?
